{{nihongo|'''Ikarashi Shrine'''|五十嵐神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Echigo Province]].

'''Ikarashi Shrine''' (いからしじんじゃ) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|abstract|Q845945|ar|جينجا|arz|ضريح شنتو|bcl|Shinto shrine|ca|Jinja|cs|Šintoistická svatyně|da|Shinto-tempel|de|Shintō-Schrein|el|Σιντοϊστικό Ιερό|eo|Ŝintoa sanktejo|es|Jinja|eu|Jinja|fa|معبد شینتویی|fi|Šintolainen pyhäkkö|fr|Sanctuaire shinto|hi|शिंतो मंदिर|hr|Šintoistički hram|hu|Sintó szentély|id|Jinja|it|Jinja|ja|神社|ka|ძინძია|ko|신사 (신토)|lb|Shintō-Schräin|mr|शिंतो मंदिर|nl|Jinja (heiligdom)|no|Jinja|or|ଜିଞ୍ଜା|pl|Jinja|pt|Templo xintoísta|ru|Дзиндзя|sc|Jinja|simple|Shinto shrine|sl|Šintoistično svetišče|sr|Шинтоистички храм|sv|Jinja|th|ศาลเจ้าชินโต|tok|tomo sewi pi nasin sewi Sinto|tr|Şinto tapınağı|uk|Святилище (синто)|uz|Dzindzya|vi|Thần xã|wuu|神社|zh|神社|zh_yue|神社|qid=Q845945}} located in Iida, {{ill|Sanjō, Niigata|Q817273|qid=Q817273}}, {{ill|Niigata Prefecture|Q132705|qid=Q132705}}. It is a {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shikinaisha}} (minor shrine). Under the {{ill|Q712534|lt=former shrine rank}}, it was classified as a prefectural shrine.

=== Overview ===
It is identified with the “Ikarashi Shrine” listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932}} under {{ill|Echigo Province|be|Этыго (правінцыя)|ckb|پارێزگای ئێچیگۆ|cs|Provincie Ečigo|de|Provinz Echigo|es|Provincia de Echigo|fa|ولایت اچیگو|fr|Province d'Echigo|gl|Provincia de Echigo|id|Provinsi Echigo|it|Echigo|ja|越後国|ko|에치고국|lt|Ečigo žemė|nl|Echigo (provincie)|pt|Província de Echigo|ru|Этиго (провинция)|simple|Echigo Province|sk|Ečigo (provincia)|sr|Провинција Ечиго|tr|Echigo (vilayet)|uk|Провінція Етіґо|zh|越後國|zh_min_nan|Etigo-kok|zh_yue|越後國|qid=Q666514}}, {{ill|Kanbara district|Q11621281|qid=Q11621281}}. In the early modern period, it was also known as “Wakaichioji” and “Iida Shrine.” The enshrined deity is {{ill|Prince Ikatarashihiko|Q11372186|qid=Q11372186|lt=Ikaruhi Obi-hiko no Mikoto}}. According to tradition, {{ill|Prince Ikatarashihiko|Q11372186|qid=Q11372186|lt=Ikaruhi Obi-hiko no Mikoto}} resided in the area of Miyazawa, taught flood control and agricultural techniques, and led the development of the Shimoda region; it is also said that the name of the {{ill|Ikarashi river|Q11372110|qid=Q11372110}} derives from this. The annual festival is held on {{ill|May 3|Q2547|qid=Q2547}}. As for candidate shrines ({{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=ronsya}}) for Ikarashi Shrine, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Yagi Shrine}} in Kitaiogawa of the same city is also cited, but many theories support this shrine.

Today the shrine is located on a hill overlooking the Ikarashi River, but it is presumed that in the medieval period it stood at the {{ill|Kimon|Q11673539|qid=Q11673539}} (northeast, unlucky direction) of the residence of a local powerful clan, the manor of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ikarashi Kobunji}}, which was situated at the foot of the hill.

Within the shrine grounds is the Shimekake Ōsugi (sacred rope-hung giant cedar), which carries a legend that a huge stone thrown from the garden of Ikarashi Kobunji Yoshitatsu’s residence became embedded in the cedar. It was revered because drinking a decoction made from its bark was believed to ensure safe childbirth. It was designated a {{ill|Natural monument|Q23790|qid=Q23790}} of Niigata Prefecture in {{ill|Shōwa era|Q327567|qid=Q327567}} 29 ({{ill|1954|Q18581|qid=Q18581}}), but after being damaged by the {{ill|Typhoon Nancy (1961)|Q1140009|qid=Q1140009}} in 36 ({{ill|1961|Q3696|qid=Q3696}}) and dying, the designation was revoked.<ref>{{Citation|Japanese book|title=Kadokawa Dictionary of Japanese Place Names 15|year=1989|pages=126–127|chapter=Ikarashi Shrine|publisher={{ill|Kadokawa Shoten|Q1054765|qid=Q1054765}}|editor=Editorial Committee of “Kadokawa Dictionary of Japanese Place Names”|isbn=4-04-001150-3}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|Japanese book|title=Comprehensive History of Japanese Place Names, Vol. 15|year=1986|page=651|contribution=Ikarashi Shrine|publisher={{ill|Heibonsha|Q11482108|qid=Q11482108}}|isbn=4-582-49015-8}}</ref>.

'''Address'''
* 2283 Iida, Sanjo City, Niigata Prefecture
'''Access'''
*By car
** About 40 minutes by car from {{ill|Hokuriku Expressway|Q1549512|qid=Q1549512}} {{ill|Sanjo-Tsubame interchange|Q10866197|qid=Q10866197|lt=Sanjo-Tsubame IC}}
*By bus
** From {{ill|Higashi-Sanjō Station|Q5753817|qid=Q5753817}}, take the {{ill|Echigo Kotsu|Q11636491|qid=Q11636491}} bus bound for “{{ill|Yagigahana|Q65249077|qid=Q65249077}} Onsen,” get off after about 30 minutes at “Shimoda Junior High School-mae,” then walk 20 minutes
